advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Only raise AcliNotInstalledError when acli is genuinely unresolvable; re-raise the original FileNotFoundError otherwise instead of unconditionally relabeling it.
evidence: require_acli returns silently when acli_binary_available(base) is True (line 193-194), so the trailing raise executes for FileNotFoundErrors whose cause is NOT a missing acli binary.
advisory.finding: In the _run_acli FileNotFoundError handler, when require_acli(base) does NOT raise (acli is resolvable), control falls through to unconditionally `raise AcliNotInstalledError(errno.ENOENT, str(exc))`, mislabeling an unrelated FileNotFoundError (e.g. a nonexistent cwd, or a different missing file referenced by the spawn) as 'acli not installed'. The re-raise should only apply when acli is genuinely missing.
scenarios: A FileNotFoundError from Popen due to an invalid cwd or other spawn-time missing file while acli itself is on PATH — operator is told to install acli, masking the true fault.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the handler, call require_acli(base) (which raises when missing); if it returns, `raise` (re-raise the original exc) rather than constructing an AcliNotInstalledError.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard acli_binary_available/require_acli against an empty acli_cmd list.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:184: `exe = (acli_cmd if acli_cmd is not None else _DEFAULT_ACLI_CMD)[0]`
An empty list is not None, so it bypasses the default and indexes [0] on an empty list -> IndexError.
advisory.finding: acli_binary_available treats acli_cmd as always having a non-empty first element via `acli_cmd[0]`; an empty list passed as acli_cmd would raise IndexError rather than a clean False/typed error.
scenarios: A caller passing acli_cmd=[] (e.g. misconfiguration) crashes with IndexError instead of a meaningful error.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the DC-transport source grep with a behavioral/import check (e.g. assert the acli transport module is absent from sys.modules after importing the DC transport, or that spawning DC ops never invokes acli).
evidence: tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_preflight_missing_binary.py:145-148: `with open(src, encoding="utf-8") as fh: text = fh.read()` then `assert 'Popen(["acli"' not in text` and `assert "_DEFAULT_ACLI_CMD" not in text`
Docstring claim (line 136-137) is 'resolves without importing the Cloud acli subprocess transport' but the assertion greps two literal strings in the source, not the module's imports.

search_files over jira_datacenter/transport.py for 'Popen' returned (no matches) — so both asserted strings are already absent regardless of any real acli dependency, making the grep unable to distinguish a clean DC path from one that acquired acli by another spelling.
advisory.finding: test_data_center_path_does_not_import_acli_transport asserts on the DC transport SOURCE TEXT (`'Popen(["acli"' not in text` and `'_DEFAULT_ACLI_CMD' not in text`) rather than on behavior/imports. It is a source-grep whose absence check is a fail-open oracle: it passes both when the DC path truly has no acli dependency AND when the DC path shells out to acli in ANY other syntactic form (e.g. `subprocess.run(["acli", ...])`, `Popen(acli_cmd)`, or `from ..jira.acli_subprocess import ...`). The docstring claims it verifies the DC transport 'resolves without importing the Cloud acli subprocess transport', but no import is actually checked.
advisory.suggested_fix: Import the DC transport, then assert `'rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.acli_subprocess' not in sys.modules` (or introspect dc_transport module's referenced names) instead of grepping the file text.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that passes acli_cmd with an explicit path (e.g. absolute path to the stub, and a non-existent absolute path) to cover the has_sep branch of acli_binary_available.
evidence: Added lines: `has_sep = os.sep in exe or (os.altsep is not None and os.altsep in exe)` and `if has_sep: return os.path.isfile(exe) and os.access(exe, os.X_OK)`

Named violating input: `acli_binary_available(['/nonexistent/acli'])` should return False and `acli_binary_available([str(existing_stub_path)])` should return True — neither the separator-present nor the os.access-fails case is exercised by any test in the file.
ABSENCE: no test passes an acli_cmd whose element[0] contains a path separator.
advisory.finding: The newly-added explicit-path branch of acli_binary_available (when the binary name contains os.sep/os.altsep it checks os.path.isfile + os.access rather than shutil.which) has no test. All tests use the bare-name 'acli' which only exercises the shutil.which branch.
